design_summary: Synthesizable FPGA supervisory top for an external NVIDIA DoMINO Automotive Aero reference service. The top provides compact request/response streaming transport, a firmware-visible CSR/MMIO control plane, protocol validation, timeout/freshness/sequence checking, bounded outstanding message handling, actuator command clamping, and explicit fault reporting. The RTL does not implement surrogate model computation, geometry processing, CFD, or tensor operations; it only supervises transport and safe actuator command issuance.

fixed_assumptions: Top-level request payload width is compact and bounded to 128 bits.
Top-level response payload width is compact and bounded to 128 bits.
CSR/MMIO data path is 64 bits or less.
Outstanding request buffering, if used, is small and BRAM-friendly.
Any external model execution occurs outside RTL; the RTL only supervises transport and actuation.
No fallback command is silently substituted on invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions; actuator validity is deasserted and faults are latched for software handling.

feature_contracts.description: After reset, the controller shall not present a valid actuator command and the fault outputs shall be in their reset-visible baseline until configuration and enable are written validly.
A valid MMIO write to CONTROL shall update enable and mode_select semantic outputs that the controller consumes.
When enabled with a valid configuration and the external request side is ready, the controller shall drive a request payload and request-valid output.
When the controller is waiting for a response, it shall drive response-ready toward the external service.
If a validated response requests an actuator command outside the programmed min/max range, the command shall be saturated and clamp_event asserted.
An invalid, stale, or sequence-mismatched response shall latch a fault and inhibit actuator command validity.
Firmware can read status through the MMIO interface and receive a ready response from the CSR block.

top_module.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
top_module.description: Top-level supervisory FPGA IP integrating CSR/MMIO, request generation, response validation, bounded buffering, timeout/freshness monitoring, and actuator command gating for an external aero reference service.
top_module.functionality: Implements a real-time active-aerodynamics controller supervisor. The top decodes CSR/MMIO writes and reads, issues compact model requests with sequence and age tokens, accepts compact model responses, validates opcode/sequence/age/integrity, clamps actuator commands to programmed bounds with optional slew limiting, tracks timeout and freshness, optionally buffers a bounded number of outstanding requests in BRAM, and asserts explicit fault/status outputs. The top never implements the reference service itself and never assumes predictions are valid after reset. On invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions, actuator_cmd_valid is deasserted and the fault is latched for software handling; no silent substitute command is emitted.
responsibilities: Provide firmware-visible CSR/MMIO register access with address, write-data, read-data, valid, write-enable, and ready/response semantics.
Generate external request transactions with valid/data and accept ready from the reference service.
Accept external response transactions with valid/data and emit ready to the reference service.
Encode and track sequence numbers, timestamps/age tokens, selected operating point, and geometry reference handle IDs in request payloads.
Validate response sequence match, opcode validity, optional integrity bits, freshness, timeout, and packet length consistency.
Clamp actuator commands to programmed min/max limits and optionally limit slew against the previously accepted command.
Latch and report faults explicitly until cleared by software.
Use a small bounded buffer for outstanding request tracking when enabled.
Drive only compact, implementation-friendly ports and avoid exposing large geometry or flow arrays.
top_module.reset_behavior: On reset, the request interface is deasserted, response ready is driven low or held in a safe non-accepting state until configuration is valid, actuator_cmd_valid is deasserted, fault_status is cleared to the reset-visible baseline, clamp_event is cleared, and fallback_active is deasserted. No actuator command is driven as valid during reset. Configuration registers must be written and enable asserted before normal operation can begin.
behavior_rules: All module-to-module and top-level user-visible control signals shall be synthesizable RTL signals with no hidden behavior.
The top-level request payload width shall not exceed 128 bits and the response payload width shall not exceed 128 bits.
The CSR/MMIO interface shall implement reachable decode for every declared register field in register_contract.
If enable is not asserted or configuration is invalid, the top shall inhibit actuator_cmd_valid and remain in a non-issuing state.

The controller FSM shall include RESET, IDLE, ISSUE_REQUEST, WAIT_RESPONSE, VALIDATE_RESPONSE, APPLY_COMMAND, SAFE_FALLBACK, and FAULT_HOLD states, with RESET as the power-on state and FAULT_HOLD used for latched-fault containment.
No fallback command substitution is permitted; on invalid or stale data the command validity is deasserted and the fault latched instead.
Response validation shall include sequence match, timeout/freshness limit, opcode validity, optional integrity/parity if the packed format includes it, and packet length/format checks.

When a response command exceeds programmed bounds, it shall be saturated to the configured min/max range and clamp_event asserted, but actuator_cmd_valid shall only be asserted for a valid accepted command path.
Outstanding request tracking, if enabled, shall be limited to a small bounded queue suitable for FPGA BRAM inference.
The request payload shall include sequence number, age/timestamp token, operating point, and geometry reference handle/ID fields.
The response payload shall include sequence number, opcode, command field, and optional integrity/status fields used by validation.
Faults shall remain latched until software clears them through the CSR/MMIO interface and re-enables the controller.
All top-level outputs must have real RTL drivers; no output may be tied only to a child input.

modules.name: aero_csr_mmio
modules.description: Firmware-visible register block and decode logic for control, status, configuration, and fault clear operations. It presents a synchronous single-cycle or wait-stated MMIO interface and produces explicit semantic control outputs for the controller FSM while returning status and register contents on reads.
modules.functionality: Implements the full firmware control-plane contract. All declared registers are reachable through decode and are reflected in the register_contract. It exposes enable, mode selection, timeout/freshness limits, command bounds, slew limit, request sequence seed, operating point, geometry reference ID, safe actuator command value, and fault clear. It also returns status fields from the controller. Reads and writes are synchronous and may use a single-cycle ready or wait-state protocol.
responsibilities: Decode firmware read/write transactions.
Expose all control and status registers required by the top-level contract.
Generate semantic configuration outputs for the controller.
Capture controller status inputs for readback.
Provide explicit fault-clear control.
Maintain software-visible register accessibility for all declared fields.
modules.reset_behavior: All writable configuration registers reset to safe defaults. Readback returns reset-visible values after reset deassertion. Ready is deasserted during reset and may be held low until the interface is initialized. Fault clear is deasserted on reset.
behavior_rules: Every register named in the register_contract shall be reachable through decode.
The module shall not invent inaccessible software-visible state.
Status readback shall reflect the controller status inputs that are provided to it.
The MMIO response path shall be deterministic and synthesizable.
No transport bus reuse is permitted to hide semantic fields; the semantic outputs are explicit ports.

modules.name: aero_request_response_controller
modules.description: Core control FSM for request issuance, response validation, timeout tracking, command clamping, fault latching, and bounded request buffering. It consumes explicit semantic configuration from the CSR block and drives the external request/response transport and actuator command outputs.
modules.functionality: Implements the control FSM with states RESET, IDLE, ISSUE_REQUEST, WAIT_RESPONSE, VALIDATE_RESPONSE, APPLY_COMMAND, SAFE_FALLBACK, and FAULT_HOLD. It packages requests using sequence number, age/timestamp token, selected operating point, and geometry reference handle, writes and reads a small bounded request buffer in technology-neutral BRAM terms, validates response opcode/sequence/freshness/length/integrity, clamps commands within programmed bounds, applies optional slew limiting, latches faults, and inhibits actuator validity on invalid conditions. It never substitutes a silent fallback command; instead it deasserts actuator_cmd_valid when invalid and reports faults explicitly.
responsibilities: Drive the request transport outputs.
Consume the response transport inputs.
Generate bounded actuator commands only when validated.
Track sequence numbers, age, timeout, and freshness.
Emit explicit fault and clamp status.
Interface to the small bounded memory macro for outstanding message storage.
Ensure safe inhibition rather than substitute command emission on invalid or faulted conditions.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, the FSM enters RESET then IDLE only after internal initialization. Request valid is deasserted, response ready is deasserted or held safe, actuator_cmd_valid is deasserted, status_last_seq_seen is cleared to the configured seed or reset baseline, fault_status is cleared to reset-visible baseline, and no command is emitted as valid until configuration and enable are valid.
behavior_rules: The FSM shall contain at least the required states RESET, IDLE, ISSUE_REQUEST, WAIT_RESPONSE, VALIDATE_RESPONSE, APPLY_COMMAND, SAFE_FALLBACK, and FAULT_HOLD.
On enable with valid configuration, the controller packages a request and issues it through the external request transport.
The controller shall validate response sequence, opcode, age/timeout, and integrity/length fields as applicable to the packed format.
If any validation fails or timeout expires, the controller shall assert fault_status and inhibit actuator_cmd_valid.
Commands shall be clamped to the programmed min/max range and optional slew limits; clamp_event shall assert on clamp occurrence.
No silent substitute command shall be driven on invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions.
The bounded memory interface shall remain technology-neutral so the FPGA flow can map it to native block RAM.
The output command shall never exceed programmed limits.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_msg_fifo_bram
modules.description: Memory macro interface module derived from memory_macros.
responsibilities: Expose the memory macro interface for RTL generation and downstream collateral.
modules.reset_behavior: Memory macro contents are not reset by the controller reset.
behavior_rules: Preserve the declared memory macro port interface.

top_level_connections.description: Global synchronous clock fanout to the CSR/MMIO block and the controller FSM.
Active-low synchronous reset fanout to all submodules.
External request-ready handshake input into the controller.
External response-valid handshake input into the controller.
External response payload input into the controller.
Firmware MMIO address input into the CSR/register block.
Firmware MMIO write-data input into the CSR/register block.
Firmware MMIO transaction-valid input into the CSR/register block.
Firmware MMIO write-enable input into the CSR/register block.
Firmware MMIO read-data output driven by the CSR/register block.
Firmware MMIO ready/response output driven by the CSR/register block.
External request-valid output driven by the controller.
External request payload output driven by the controller.
External response-ready output driven by the controller.
Top-level actuator command output driven by the controller.
Top-level actuator command-valid output driven by the controller.
Top-level explicit fault status output driven by the controller.
Top-level clamp-event status output driven by the controller.
Top-level fallback-active indicator driven by the controller as a no-command-valid safe inhibit indication.
